name: Effectual Calling and Regeneration

objectives.text: Identify from Ezekiel that God promises to give His people a new heart in place of a heart of stone
Retell Jesus' conversation with Nicodemus and name being born again as something God does
Explain using Paul's picture of being dead in sin why people cannot make themselves spiritually alive
Describe how Jesus compares the Spirit's work in the new birth to the wind that blows where it wishes
Retell how the Lord opened Lydia's heart to pay attention to Paul's preaching
Define regeneration as the Spirit's work of giving new spiritual life and distinguish it from a person trying to become better
Recite the Shorter Catechism definition of effectual calling and identify its four parts
Compare the outward call of the gospel to all who hear with the inward effectual call of the Spirit
Explain how God uses the preached word as the ordinary means by which He effectually calls and gives new birth
Analyze the tradition's teaching that regeneration is monergistic, the work of God alone in which the sinner is passive
Identify the marks John gives of those who have been born of God
Interpret Paul's language of being made alive together with Christ while dead in trespasses
Analyze Paul's description of the natural person to explain why an inward work of the Spirit is needed for anyone to receive the gospel
Trace the Old Testament promises of heart renewal to Jesus' teaching on being born of water and the Spirit
Explain from Scripture why the Reformed tradition holds that regeneration precedes and produces faith
Explain why the Canons of Dort place the fault of rejecting the gospel call on the hearer rather than on the gospel or on God
Construct an account of effectual calling from Paul's teaching in Romans 8 and related texts
Explain how the confessions describe the Spirit as renewing the human will rather than forcing it
Defend from John 3 the necessity of the new birth for seeing and entering the kingdom of God
Evaluate the view that a person's decision causes the new birth against the Reformed teaching of sovereign regeneration
Evaluate the doctrine of baptismal regeneration in light of Scripture and the Westminster Confession's teaching on the sacrament and the Spirit
Explain the Westminster Confession's teaching on how the Spirit regenerates elect persons who are incapable of being outwardly called by the word
Analyze how Reformed theologians have related effectual calling and regeneration to each other and to the beginning of the order of salvation

changes: Kept and reworded the real competencies: new heart, born again, the wind of the Spirit, effectual calling, outward and inward call, Lydia, monergism, made alive with Christ, regeneration preceding faith, Romans 8, decisional regeneration, the necessity of the new birth, and the order of salvation. Recast 'we cannot save ourselves' as spiritual death to keep it on regeneration. Moved Lydia to an earlier retelling objective and dropped the vague 'apply' wording. Merged 'connect regeneration to the Spirit' into the monergism and wind objectives. Added objectives on the Shorter Catechism definition, the word as the means of calling, the marks of the new birth in 1 John, the inability of the natural person, Old Testament heart renewal promises, hearer responsibility (Canons III/IV.8-9), the will renewed rather than forced, baptismal regeneration, and WCF 10.3. Replaced whole-chapter references with verse ranges and added WCF, WLC, Heidelberg and Dort citations where they state the doctrine.
